subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept replacing Node fs.glob with the internal yielding walker on the bootstrap-context path, given the compatibility tests and remaining lack of full live channel proof?
rationale: The patch appears correct and keeps SDK signatures stable, but the glob resolution engine and bootstrap hook scheduling are compatibility-sensitive runtime behavior that maintainers should explicitly own before merge.

options.title: Accept after exact-head gates
options.body: Proceed once required checks pass on the reviewed head, treating the direct loader liveness proof plus focused compatibility tests as sufficient for this internal runtime fix.

options.title: Require full embedded-run proof
options.body: Ask for a live embedded_run/channel proof that shows keepalives or queued I/O stay responsive during bootstrap-context before merge.

options.title: Defer to a narrower core change
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want a smaller change that only removes the synchronous read/glob stall without taking ownership of the local glob matching semantics yet.

recommendation.title: Accept after exact-head gates
recommendation.body: Proceed once required checks pass on the reviewed head, treating the direct loader liveness proof plus focused compatibility tests as sufficient for this internal runtime fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history across the bootstrap workspace, hook, and embedded-runner surfaces being changed.
